title: Enhanced CPD & lifelong learning
blurb: The GDC's Enhanced CPD scheme for dental nurses: hours, verifiable evidence, development outcomes, recommended topics and your annual statement.
question: A newly registered colleague plans to "do all 50 hours in the last year" of her cycle and asks whether reading journal articles and an in-house training session will count. What would you tell her about the hours rule, what counts as verifiable CPD and what records she must keep?

teach.h: Why CPD is part of being registered
teach.body: Continuing professional development (CPD) is learning, training or other activity that maintains and develops your practice and is relevant to your field. Guidance, materials and technology keep changing, so learning never stops when you qualify. CPD is a legal requirement of GDC registration because it assures the public that you keep your skills up to date. The rules are set in law (the CPD rules), which give the GDC powers to act if a registrant does not comply.

items.label: minimum in every 2 consecutive CPD years
CPD year runs 1 August to 31 July

teach.caption: You must not declare two zero-hour years in a row. Cramming 50 hours into the final year breaks the 10-hour rule.
Plan with your PDP, do verifiable activity across the cycle, reflect on its impact on patients and your practice, and record it in your log.

teach.body: Every hour you declare to the GDC must be verifiable, which means you hold documentary evidence from the provider. It must show the subject, aims and objectives, the anticipated development outcomes, the date, the hours, your name, who quality-assures it, and confirmation it is accurate. It should also show your GDC number. In-house training can count if it meets these requirements. The GDC does not approve any CPD providers, so it is up to you to check. Non-verifiable learning, such as reading a journal, is still useful but isn't declared.

rows.label: E-learning with a certificate showing aims, outcomes and hours
In-house session with documented aims, objectives, outcomes and evidence
Lecture with no certificate or documentation
Reading a journal article at home

teach.note: Breaks and travel time never count towards your hours.

head: Outcome
Covers
Example CPD
rows: Communication with patients and the team
Managing yourself and others, teamwork, leadership
Knowledge and skills in your field
teach.caption: Every planned and completed activity must link to at least one outcome. Covering all four in a cycle is encouraged.

items.label: Radiography
items.sub: And radiation protection, if you take radiographs

teach.caption: Recommended, not compulsory. Other recommended topics: legal and ethical issues, complaints handling, oral cancer early detection, and safeguarding children and vulnerable adults. The GDC keeps the live list on its website.

teach.body: Your CPD record has three parts: your PDP, a log of completed activity, and the evidence. The log shows the title, date, hours, development outcomes and that you reflected. Keep evidence for the whole cycle and five years after it, as the GDC can sample records up to five years after a cycle ends. Each year you make an annual CPD statement on eGDC, declaring your hours and that you have a PDP and a CPD record. You, not your employer, are responsible. Failing to make your statement or meet the requirements puts your registration at risk.

items.label: CPD year starts
items.sub: Your first cycle starts the 1 August after you register

items.label: Renewal opens on eGDC
items.sub: About six weeks before the year ends

items.label: CPD year ends
items.sub: CPD done after this can't count for this year

items.label: Last day to make the statement
items.sub: 28 days after the year ends; miss it and registration is at risk

teach.caption: If you take time off the register, keep doing CPD and check the GDC's requirements before you return.

teach.text: "10 hours" is NOT the cycle total. Dental nurses need 50 verifiable hours per 5-year cycle; 10 hours is the minimum in every two consecutive CPD years.

items: 50 verifiable hours per 5-year cycle, at least 10 hours in every 2 consecutive years.
CPD year 1 August to 31 July; annual statement on eGDC by 28 August; missing it puts registration at risk.
Verifiable = provider evidence with aims, outcomes, date, hours, QA. In-house can count; no certificate, no credit.
Outcomes: A communication, B management and teamwork, C knowledge and skills, D professionalism.
Recommended (not compulsory): medical emergencies 10 h (2 h every year), decontamination 5 h, radiography 5 h, plus legal and ethical issues, complaints, oral cancer and safeguarding.
Record = PDP + log + evidence; keep for the cycle plus five years. You are responsible, not your employer.

summary: You can now state the Enhanced CPD hours for dental nurses and the 10-hour rule, explain what makes CPD verifiable, map activities to development outcomes A to D, name the recommended topics, and describe the CPD record, the annual statement and what happens if you don't comply.

A.q: How many hours of verifiable CPD must a dental nurse complete in each five-year cycle?
A.why: Dental nurses must complete at least 50 hours of verifiable CPD in each five-year cycle.

whyNot.0: Ten hours is the minimum in every two consecutive years, not the cycle total.
whyNot.2: Seventy-five hours applies to hygienists, therapists, orthodontic therapists and clinical dental technicians.
whyNot.3: One hundred hours applies to dentists.

A.q: A dental nurse attends a lecture but receives no certificate or other documentation. Why can't it count as verifiable CPD?
options: It lasted for less than one full hour
It wasn't delivered or approved by the GDC
Lectures can never be counted as verifiable
No documentary evidence from the provider
A.why: Verifiable CPD requires documentary evidence from the provider showing aims, outcomes, hours and quality assurance.

whyNot.0: Length isn't the issue; without evidence, no hours can be verified.
whyNot.1: The GDC doesn't deliver or approve CPD providers.
whyNot.2: Lectures can count if the provider gives the required evidence.

A.q: A dental nurse completes a course on new impression materials. Which development outcome does it most likely map to?
A.why: Outcome C covers maintaining and developing knowledge and skills within your field of practice, such as materials.

whyNot.0: Outcome A covers communication, such as consent and complaints.
whyNot.1: Outcome B covers management of self and others, teamwork and leadership.
whyNot.3: Outcome D covers behaviours that maintain patient confidence, such as ethics and law.

B.q: A dental nurse has done no CPD in the first two years of their cycle. Which requirement have they failed to meet?
options: At least 10 hours in every two-year period
At least 5 hours of radiography each year
An annual appraisal with their employer
B.why: The GDC requires at least 10 hours of CPD in every two consecutive CPD years, and you can't declare two zero years in a row.

whyNot.1: Fifty hours is the five-year total, not a yearly requirement.
whyNot.2: Radiography is a recommended topic (5 hours per cycle), not a yearly requirement.
whyNot.3: Appraisal is good practice but isn't a GDC CPD rule.

B.q: When does the CPD year run for dental care professionals, including dental nurses?
B.why: For dental care professionals, the CPD year matches the registration year: 1 August to 31 July.

whyNot.0: 1 January to 31 December is the CPD year for dentists.
whyNot.1: This is the financial year, not the GDC's CPD year.
whyNot.3: This is the academic year, not the GDC's CPD year.

B.q: A nurse assumes their employer will arrange all the CPD they need. Who is responsible for a registrant's CPD?
B.why: Each registrant is personally responsible for planning, completing and recording their own CPD.

whyNot.1: Employers may support CPD, but responsibility stays with the registrant.
whyNot.2: The manager may help organise training, but isn't responsible for your compliance.
whyNot.3: The GDC sets and checks the rules; it doesn't do your CPD for you.

C.q: Which topic does the GDC recommend dental nurses cover in every CPD cycle?
C.why: Medical emergencies is a GDC recommended topic: at least 10 hours per cycle and at least 2 hours every year.

whyNot.0: Implant placement is outside a dental nurse's scope and isn't a recommended topic.
whyNot.1: Wire bending is a technical skill, not a GDC recommended topic.
whyNot.2: Accounting isn't a GDC recommended topic.

C.q: The GDC asks to see a dental nurse's CPD record. How long should CPD evidence be kept?
options: For one year after each course ends
The current cycle and 5 years after it
Only until the annual statement is made
For the whole of their working life
C.why: Evidence must be kept for the whole cycle and for five years after it ends, because the GDC can sample records during that time.

whyNot.0: One year is too short; the GDC can check years later.
whyNot.2: Statements don't end the need to keep evidence.
whyNot.3: This goes beyond the GDC's requirement.

C.q: A dental nurse reads a journal article in their own time and makes notes. How should this be treated?
options: As verifiable CPD, if they keep the notes
As outcome D verifiable CPD automatically
As non-verifiable CPD that isn't declared
As evidence for their appraisal only
C.why: Reading without provider evidence is non-verifiable. It's still valuable learning, but only verifiable hours are declared to the GDC.

whyNot.0: Your own notes aren't provider evidence, so it can't be verifiable.
whyNot.1: No activity is automatically verifiable; it needs provider evidence.
whyNot.3: It can inform appraisal, but the key point is that it isn't declared as CPD hours.

reteach.title: Jade's five-year cycle
reteach.question: Jade registered in March and wants to stay on track without a last-minute panic. What does a sensible cycle look like?

blocks.body: Jade's first CPD cycle starts on the 1 August after she registers. She writes a PDP, then does a little verifiable CPD every year: medical emergencies each year, plus decontamination, radiography and a communication course along the way. After each course she writes a short reflection and saves the certificate. Every summer she makes her annual statement on eGDC by 28 August. Over five years she passes 50 hours and never has a two-year gap below 10.

blocks.caption: Every pair of consecutive years adds up to at least 10 hours, and the cycle total is over 50.

blocks.text: 50 hours in Year 5 alone would still fail: Years 1 and 2 (and 3 and 4) would each total zero.

explain.body: 50 verifiable hours per 5-year cycle, and at least 10 hours in every two consecutive CPD years. If you do 3 hours one year, you need at least 7 the next.

test.q: A dental nurse declares 3 hours of CPD in one year. What is the minimum they must declare the following year?
test.why: At least 10 hours are needed across any two consecutive years, so 3 + 7 = 10.

whyNot.2: 10 would be more than enough, but the minimum is 7.

explain.body: Declared CPD must be backed by provider evidence. In-house training can count if it has aims, objectives, outcomes and documented evidence.

test.q: Which detail is NOT required on evidence for verifiable CPD?
options: The price paid for the course
test.why: The cost of a course has nothing to do with whether it's verifiable.

whyNot.3: Quality assurance details must be shown.

explain.body: Every activity links to at least one outcome. A: communication. B: managing self and others, teamwork, leadership. C: knowledge and skills. D: behaviours that maintain patient confidence.

test.q: A dental nurse completes training on working effectively within the dental team. Which outcome does it map to?
test.why: Outcome B covers effective management of self and others and working with the dental team.

whyNot.0: Outcome A is about communication, such as consent and complaints.
whyNot.2: Outcome C is about clinical and technical knowledge and skills.
whyNot.3: Outcome D is about ethics, law and professional behaviours.

explain.body: Make an annual CPD statement on eGDC (by 28 August for the year ending 31 July). Keep your PDP, log and evidence for the cycle and five years after. Missing a statement, or ignoring the GDC's 28-day notice, puts your registration at risk.

test.q: A dental nurse fails to make their annual CPD statement and ignores the GDC's notice. What is the likely consequence?
options: A small fine added to next year's fee
An automatic extra 10 hours to complete
No consequence if their hours are done
Their registration is put at risk
test.why: The GDC sends a notice with 28 days to respond. Not making the statement or not responding puts the nurse's registration at risk.

whyNot.0: The GDC's CPD guidance describes no fines; the risk is to the nurse's registration.
whyNot.1: The guidance sets no automatic extra-hours penalty.
whyNot.2: The statement is itself a requirement, even if the hours are done.
